### **1. Cercli**


Cercli is an ATS with


[Cera](https://www.cercli.com/cera/) , a built-in AI hiring agent, made for lean, high-volume hiring teams. It covers the basics, from job posting to offer. The ATS syncs with LinkedIn and Indeed, so you post open roles without switching platforms.


Candidates book their own interviews, and you send offers for e-signature. A hired candidate then becomes an employee in


[Cercli’s HR system](https://www.cercli.com/hris/) in a few clicks. Cera scores every incoming resume against criteria you set. You get a ranked shortlist with each person’s strengths and gaps. Cera only recommends, and you make the final call. If you override a ranking, Cercli logs who changed it and when.


[Orin, the AI sourcing agent](https://www.cercli.com/orin/) , finds people who haven’t applied. Describe the role in plain English, with no Boolean strings, and Orin searches 900M+ profiles. You send the outreach over LinkedIn and email. Orin also connects to Claude, so a search keeps its criteria and shortlist when you switch between Orin and Claude. Both agents run inside the Cercli ATS. Switching? Import your active pipelines and past records. Not ready to leave? Add either agent to your current ATS.


#### **Pros:**


- Cercli flags stalled candidates automatically.


- Hiring managers see a flag on vague interview feedback.


- SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant.


#### **Cons:**


- Cera focuses on resume screening and doesn’t run recorded video interviews.


#### **Best for:**


Lean, high-volume SMB hiring teams that want AI screening and sourcing, plus hiring and HR on one record.


### **2. Ashby**


Ashby puts reporting inside the ATS, and it sells its analytics on their own to companies on other ATSs. It’s an all-in-one platform with structured interview plans built in. Its main AI feature, AI-Assisted Application Review, checks each applicant against criteria your recruiters set.


#### **Pros:**


- An AI report builder creates reports from a plain-English chat.


- Admins can hide other feedback until an interviewer submits their own.


#### **Cons:**


- The AI Notetaker and advanced scheduling automation are paid add-ons.


- The Foundations plan limits you to one offer template and one candidate survey.


#### **Best for:**


Startups and growth companies that want deep recruiting analytics.


### **3. Workable**


Workable pairs an ATS and an HR plan, with an optional AI agent on top. AI screening summaries show how each candidate matches your hard requirements. The optional Workable Agent also checks each inbound candidate against up to 14 job criteria.


#### **Pros:**


- Published pricing, starting at $299 a month for companies with 1 to 20 employees.


- An HR plan adds an HRIS and onboarding, with up to 20% off when you bundle.


#### **Cons:**


- Agent usage beyond the 3,000 starter credits costs extra.


- The 15-day free trial doesn’t include the Workable Agent.


#### **Best for:**


Small and mid-size teams that want published pricing and an optional AI agent.


### **4. Greenhouse**


Greenhouse is built for structured hiring that holds up across locations and brands. Its Core plan includes a sourcing CRM and scheduling, and Plus adds multi-brand job boards. Every plan has AI tools, such as job post and interview question suggestions. Voice AI, a separate product, runs two-way voice interviews with your own questions and scoring.


#### **Pros:**


- Structured interview kits and scorecards keep every interviewer assessing the same criteria.


- Greenhouse Notetaker records and transcribes interviews, then maps AI notes to your scorecard questions.


#### **Cons:**


- Sourcing Automation needs the Plus plan or above.


- Notetaker covers video interviews only.


#### **Best for:**


Teams that want structured hiring across locations and brands.


### **5. Teamtailor**


Teamtailor builds the careers site into the ATS, with drag-and-drop content blocks. You can publish a job ad to job boards and social channels in one click. Teamtailor AI drafts job ads and summarizes resumes and video interviews. It also assesses candidates against criteria you set.


#### **Pros:**


- AI is included with unlimited usage.


- Plans come with unlimited job postings and unlimited users.


#### **Cons:**


- Candidate suggestions come from your existing database.


- Requisition approval flows and multi-brand management are Premium features.


#### **Best for:**


Teams that want employer branding and a built-in careers site.


### **6. Lever**


Lever builds a CRM into the ATS. The CRM supports nurture campaigns, and the ATS adds self-service scheduling and offer letters. In the core platform, Talent Fit matches candidates against criteria you customize. AI Screening by VONQ, an agent that pre-screens applicants on your careers site, is a paid add-on.


#### **Pros:**


- Unlimited AI interview transcripts and summaries are included in the core platform.


- Fraud Signals checks for suspicious candidate activity automatically in the background.


#### **Cons:**


- Candidate Insights and Onboarding are paid add-ons.


- Approval workflows for postings and offers sit on higher packages.


#### **Best for:**


Teams that want an ATS and CRM in one platform.


### **7. SmartRecruiters**


SmartRecruiters is built for high-volume hiring. It has been part of SAP SuccessFactors since SAP acquired it in September 2025. Its High Volume plan adds AI screening and conversational chat. Its AI companion, Winston, matches candidates and handles repetitive work from screening to scheduling.


#### **Pros:**


- Every plan includes offer management and onboarding.


- It also runs as a standalone ATS that connects to other HR systems.


#### **Cons:**


- The Essential plan starts at $14,995 and doesn’t include AI features.


- Advanced analytics is an add-on until the Complete plan.


#### **Best for:**


Teams with high-volume hiring, including SAP SuccessFactors users.


### **8. Tellent Recruitee**


Tellent Recruitee is collaborative hiring software. Every plan lets teammates assign tasks and leave shared notes. You can add Tellent HR later for an HRIS and performance management. AI Writer drafts emails and summarizes feedback on every plan. The Screening Assistant starts on the Advance plan with 100 credits a month, and full access needs the Optimize plan.


#### **Pros:**


- Tellent posts to 2,900+ job boards, including Indeed and Google for Jobs.


- The Matching Assistant finds past candidates in your database who fit a new role.


#### **Cons:**


- Contracts carry a minimum commitment of one year.


- Texting and WhatsApp Hiring cost extra.


#### **Best for:**


Growing teams that want collaborative hiring.


### **9. Manatal**


Manatal includes AI candidate scoring on every plan, even the entry one, and its Copilot compares and ranks candidates. AI enrichment fills in profiles from sites like LinkedIn and GitHub. You can post to free job boards and buy premium channels as paid campaigns.


#### **Pros:**


- Published pricing starts at $15 per user a month, billed annually.


- A built-in recruitment CRM tracks clients and placements for agencies.


#### **Cons:**


- Workflow automations are only available on the Enterprise and Enterprise Plus plans.


- Archived jobs still count toward your job limit until you delete them permanently.


#### **Best for:**


Small teams and agencies that want AI candidate scoring.


### **10. Zoho Recruit**


Zoho Recruit lets you start free and pay per recruiter as you grow. It has separate editions for corporate HR teams and staffing agencies. Zoho can publish to 70+ job boards, though paid boards cost extra. Zoho’s AI, Zia, writes job descriptions and summarizes candidate profiles.


#### **Pros:**


- A free plan lets you run one active job before you pay anything.


- The Enterprise plan adds advanced customization and recruitment automation.


#### **Cons:**


- Zia’s candidate matching needs the Enterprise plan.


- Learning curve for setup and customization.


#### **Best for:**


Small teams that want a free tier.


## **Why look for alternatives to Pinpoint?**


### **More AI and an Easier Setup**


Pinpoint would benefit from AI agents and AI resume review built in,


[one reviewer writes](https://www.g2.com/products/pinpoint-hq-pinpoint/reviews/pinpoint-review-12019104) , since many other platforms are adopting them. Setup was another pain point. Learning the platform was difficult and time-consuming, and a customer success manager helped.


### **Manual Work and LinkedIn Integration Issues**


Sourcing and scheduling still involve a lot of manual work,


[according to a reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/174069/Pinpoint/#Capterra___6610671/) . They also report some issues integrating with LinkedIn.


### **Prepopulated Questions and Email Visibility**


Prepopulated questions sometimes need items added or removed,


[a reviewer says](https://www.capterra.com/p/174069/Pinpoint/#Capterra___6757153/) . Interviewers seeing emails between the recruiter and the applicant was another problem, and they couldn’t figure out how to fix it.


If any of these sound familiar, the next section covers what to look for in a replacement.


## **How to Choose the Right Pinpoint Alternative**


The right pick depends on where your hiring slows down. Five questions will narrow the list.


### **How Many People Apply to a Typical Role?**


If it’s hundreds, you’ll want


[AI candidate screening](https://www.cercli.com/resources/ai-candidate-screening/) that reads every application. Cercli’s Cera ranks applications. Ashby’s AI-Assisted Application Review marks which of your criteria each applicant meets. The Workable Agent scores applicants against your job criteria. Check that it explains each score and lets you override it.


### **Do You Need People Who Haven’t Applied?**


Then sourcing matters more than screening. Cercli’s Orin and the Workable Agent search hundreds of millions of profiles, and Manatal includes a 700M+ database. Check who sends the outreach. Orin sends nothing until you do. Lever’s CRM is built for nurturing candidates you already know.


### **What Should Happen After the Offer Is Signed?**


If new hires should move into HR without retyping, check how the ATS and HRIS connect. Cercli’s ATS and HRIS read the same data live. Workable sells an HR plan alongside its ATS, and Recruitee hands hires to its Tellent HR add-on in a few clicks. Ask which fields carry over.


### **Do You Want to See Prices Upfront?**


Workable, Manatal, and Zoho Recruit publish their prices, and so does Ashby for teams of up to 100 employees. Pinpoint quotes per company, as do several of the alternatives. The comparison table shows which. Ask what the price includes. The Workable Agent runs on paid credits, and Recruitee asks for a one-year minimum.


### **How Big Is Your Hiring Operation?**


Large teams with high-volume hiring should look at SmartRecruiters. Lean teams that still hire in volume should look at Cercli. Very small teams can start with Manatal at $15 per user a month, billed annually, or Zoho Recruit’s free plan. Ask how much setup your team can take on.


## **See Cera and Orin Work on Your Next Open Role**


Looking past Pinpoint for AI resume review and less manual work in sourcing and scheduling? Cercli covers both. Cera reads and ranks every application, and Orin finds the people who haven’t applied. The agents run inside the Cercli ATS, and you make every hiring decision. Candidates book their own interviews, and a hire moves into HR on the same record in a few clicks.


[Book a demo](https://www.cercli.com/contact-us/) and bring the one role you can’t fill. You’ll see Orin search for it live, and the team will walk through how Cera screens the applicants. Or


[start a free Orin trial](https://app.cercli.com/orin/signup) .
